entry_points: mandatory_semantic_closure(graph, decision_id, max_nodes, max_edges, max_depth) -> dict
identity_and_determinism: normalize_impact_index accepts only the declared v1 schema, canonicalizes symbol/path dependencies and validation targets in lexical order, requires every target to be known, and derives index_id as a SHA-256 content identity over the canonical identity payload containing repository_tree_id and index_version.

impact_from_index canonicalizes changed symbols and paths, computes reverse dependency closures, returns sorted changed/affected symbols, paths, validation IDs, reasons, and dependency chains, and binds the result to the input repository_tree_id and index_id.
Unknown changed symbols or paths remain in uncovered_symbols or uncovered_paths and set uncovered_impact=true; an empty selected-test set is therefore not a claim of complete coverage.

mandatory_semantic_closure accepts only an authoritative decision seed and traverses only authoritative mandatory edges. It sorts each outgoing edge by kind, target, and edge ID; returns sorted node and edge IDs plus lexical shortest paths; and binds the result to the semantic graph root_id and v1 closure schema.

The selected graph/index contracts expose canonical SHA-256 content identities (graph_id/index_id), not a CID field. No CID is claimed for these slice results; the repository tree, schema, version, and canonical identity profile are bound explicitly.
fail_closed_invariants: An unsupported impact-index schema, missing repository_tree_id, unknown validation target, corrupt artifact, checksum mismatch, or forged graph/index identity fails before selection.
An unknown decision, a non-decision seed, a non-authoritative seed, a mandatory edge reaching a non-authoritative node, or max-depth/node/edge overflow raises CodeEvidenceAdapterError.
Empty dependency seeds and invalid dependency bounds raise CodeEvidenceAdapterError; unknown changed impact remains visible rather than being promoted to complete.
Neither a test selection nor a mandatory closure executes a test, proves an obligation, or authorizes mutation; those results require separate validation/proof evidence.

limitations: This task is receipt-only: it selects existing current-head canonical test-target and proof-obligation slicing and does not mutate proof_context or create a second selector.

The selected authority is bounded static graph/index analysis. It does not establish whole-CPython runtime semantics, dynamic import/reflection/native behavior, generated-code correctness, test completeness beyond indexed targets, proof truth, or a PCSM source-link artifact.

A selected validation ID is an indexed requirement, not an executable command or proof of test success. A mandatory closure identifies graph-recorded authority dependencies, not a formal theorem proof.

Determinism and coverage are bound to canonically normalized, identity-checked graph/index artifacts; arbitrary caller-supplied unordered graphs and indexes are not a canonical authority artifact under this receipt.
All identities are valid only under the bound tree, source digests, schemas/version, identity profile, and exact test inputs; any change invalidates this receipt.
The authoritative sealed suite remains unavailable because anyio is absent, so this receipt cannot promote completion despite provider-side passes.
The receipt's own canonical storage CID is unavailable because minting a self-describing CID would change its bytes.
